content.text: The run confirms the problem is confined to generated API labels plus prose blocks that are pure code, URLs, or identifiers. I’m checking the segment classifier now; the key hypothesis is that these are tagged as translatable text before the existing verbatim policy gets a chance to preserve them.

The diagnosis holds: `translateUnits` only treats verbatim strings as cacheable when a caller supplies them, but the API pipeline supplies none. As a result, identifier-only sidebar labels and code-only prose are sent to the model, rejected as source-identical, and retried forever. I’ll add an API-specific classifier that copies those units verbatim into the PO cache, with tests for identifiers, URLs, CSS declarations, and ordinary prose.

I’m making this at the API pipeline boundary, not in the generic memory: it will preserve only API-shaped technical units, while ordinary UI labels and prose remain eligible for Hungarian translation. The cheap check is the existing mocked API-build test, extended to prove those units bypass the adapter and are written as source text.

content.name: apply_patch

content.text: The focused test caught one boundary case: a list-item URL was still carrying its `- ` marker when matched. I’ll normalize that marker before technical-shape detection and rerun the same test.

content.name: apply_patch

content.text: The classifier test still has a single failing input, so I’m isolating it with a no-write expression check before changing the rule again. That keeps the repair constrained to the actual pattern mismatch.
